extracted.intended_audience: general readers, journalists, historians, PR/communications professionals and Apple enthusiasts interested in Apple media events
extracted.subtask_description: Compile or use a chronological list and descriptive record of a company's media/keynote events, including venue, format, major announcements, taglines, streaming and ticketing details. Useful for historians, journalists, and PR practitioners studying event practice and timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of press conferences vs press releases
rubrics_metrics.description: Apple Inc. has announced major new and redesigned products and upgrades through press conferences, while minor updates often happen through press releases on Apple Newsroom.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guides when to hold an event versus issuing a release: reserve in-person/streamed media events for major product introductions and redesigns; use newsroom/press release for smaller updates or follow-ups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep detailed agenda secret to create buzz
rubrics_metrics.description: The detailed agenda of the event is often kept as a secret to create buzz, and only unveiled during the event, though event taglines sometimes give hints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deliberate secrecy and teasing (short tagline hints) are used as a marketing tactic to build anticipation prior to an event.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide live streams and replays
rubrics_metrics.description: These events are usually streamed live on Apple's website and, in recent years, YouTube channel. Video replays of most Apple events since 2007 are available on Apple's 'Apple Events' podcast.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make events accessible via live stream (company site, major platforms) and archive replays or podcasts so remote audiences can view afterwards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select venue strategically (physical and virtual formats)
rubrics_metrics.description: Apple has held events at the following venues: Moscone West, Yerba Buena Center for the Arts, Bill Graham Civic Auditorium, Flint Center, McEnery Convention Center, Steve Jobs Theater (Apple Park), Brooklyn Academy of Music, and has used online-only and hybrid formats (online-only 2020–March 2022 due to the COVID-19 pandemic; both online and in-person June 2022–present).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose high-profile venues appropriate to the scale and tone of the announcement; be prepared to switch formats (online-only or hybrid) when circumstances (e.g., pandemic) require.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use event taglines as branding and hinting device
rubrics_metrics.description: Event taglines sometimes give hints (examples throughout the list: 'It's Showtime', 'Wish we could say more', 'See you on the 7th', etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Craft a short, evocative tagline to brand the event and subtly signal themes or product categories without revealing full details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invite press and time invitations appropriately
rubrics_metrics.description: Apple sent invitations to journalists on February 23, 2011, for a media event on March 2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Send media invitations with appropriate lead time; use controlled invite lists to manage coverage and attendance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordinate product demos and partner appearances
rubrics_metrics.description: Keynotes frequently include demonstrations of new products, software,and invited co-hosts or partner executives (examples: Adobe demos, Intel and Google executives appearing, partner demos to show app or content integrations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan live demos and partner appearances to showcase real-world use, technical capabilities, and industry relationships; rehearse demos to avoid on-stage failures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include entertainment and community events
rubrics_metrics.description: Many events include musical performances or 'Bash' parties (e.g., Vampire Weekend, Panic! at the Disco, OneRepublic, Weezer, Lana Del Rey, Sia).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Add entertainment elements (evening concerts, Bash parties) to increase PR value, attendee experience, and cultural cachet around the event.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manage ticketing, pricing and access (especially for developer conferences)
rubrics_metrics.description: WWDC ticket processes: ticket price examples (US$1,599 in 2012), changes to purchasing process (requiring Apple ID associated with a paid developer account), rapid sell-outs, and scholarship allocation (e.g., 150 free student tickets).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set clear ticket pricing, access rules, sales windows, and inclusion programs (scholarships); use limited ticketing to create scarcity and manage capacity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plan developer-focused content (sessions, labs) for technical conferences
rubrics_metrics.description: WWDC example: extensive technical program including hundreds of sessions and many hands-on labs (e.g., 110 lab sessions and 95 presentation sessions; thousands of developers attending).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For developer conferences, provide technical sessions, labs, and hands-on support to engage the target (developer) audience and deliver actionable guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordinate release timing for software and hardware
rubrics_metrics.description: Announcements often include release timing: software and OS versions are announced at the keynote and released in the following days or months (e.g., iOS, macOS release dates announced at WWDC or special events).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Align announcement date with realistic shipping/release schedules and communicate availability, pricing, and release windows during the event.

rubrics_metrics.name: Announce pricing, availability, and carrier/partner terms on-stage
rubrics_metrics.description: Events frequently communicate pricing, model availability dates, and commercial partnerships (examples: iPhone pricing and Cingular exclusivity; iPad pricing and launch dates).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include clear commercial details (price, SKUs, release dates, partner arrangements) in the announcement to allow press and customers to report accurately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use press releases/Newsroom for smaller updates and post-event details
rubrics_metrics.description: Minor updates often happen through press releases on Apple Newsroom; Apple Newsroom is used for press releases and follow-up information (e.g., post-event product pages, press statements).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reserve the newsroom for detail-rich, distributable materials and for follow-ups that do not require a live event.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support broad streaming accessibility across platforms
rubrics_metrics.description: Streaming access evolved over time (e.g., some keynotes initially streamed only on Safari/iOS/OS X; later expanded to Windows via Microsoft Edge and to YouTube).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure streams are broadly accessible (multiple platforms and browsers) to maximize live viewership; consider using major platforms like YouTube in addition to corporate site.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use surprise 'one more thing' / encore announcements sparingly
rubrics_metrics.description: Keynotes sometimes include an additional surprise announcement specifically for developers or the audience (example: Swift announced as a 'one more thing' during WWDC).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reserve a high-impact surprise or encore for late in the presentation to create memorable moments and additional press coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document events with reliable citations (encyclopedic practice)
rubrics_metrics.description: Many sections in the article are marked 'This section does not cite any sources.' (repeated template).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When documenting events (for encyclopedias, pressrooms or histories), include reliable citations and sources for claims, dates, and quote attribution to improve verifiability and trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manage leaks and embargoes
rubrics_metrics.description: Some product details were leaked prior to events (example: the iMac G4 was leaked the night before the event from Time Magazine; internal codenames revealed in court cases), indicating that leaks and embargoes are an operational concern.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement leak mitigation and embargo policies; be prepared to respond to or incorporate pre-release leaks into communications plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide attendee perks and swag when appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples of attendee gifts: a full-surface optical mouse was gifted to all attendees at a 2000 Macworld event; other events included promotional items or demos for press/attendees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offer branded swag, gifts or exclusive items sparingly to reward attendees and generate additional publicity.
